# `cis_extensions.cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection` — version 1.2

Source: `presets/cis/cloud-sql-iam-and-deletion-protection.satz`

## Purpose

CIS 5.0 §6.6 / §6.9 — Cloud SQL instances sign database users in through IAM,
and cannot be deleted while deletion protection is on. Both are new in 5.0.

Two custom constraints on `sqladmin.googleapis.com/Instance`, each enforced by a
policy on the organisation. A custom constraint is checked when an instance is
created or updated, never against one that exists: an existing instance that
breaks either is refused its next update, until that update fixes it.

IAM database authentication is a database flag — `cloudsql.iam_authentication`
on PostgreSQL, `cloudsql_iam_authentication` on MySQL. SQL Server has no such
flag, and the IAM constraint lets SQL Server instances through.

Opt-in because every Cloud SQL create and update in the organisation must then
carry both settings; tooling that creates instances without them fails.
Prowler has no check for either control, so report-compliance verifies them
through the two policies only.

## Use it

```
params {
  cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection = true
}

use "presets/cis/cloud-sql-iam-and-deletion-protection.satz" when cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection
```

`cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `CIS_GCP_Foundation_4_0`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `customer_organization_id` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

## Params

_None — the pack takes everything from the estate's params._

## Notices

What to run once this pack is switched on. satz shows each notice when the pack goes on and until the estate binds its param `true`; every command that writes to the organisation refuses while one whose severity is `error` is open.

| param | run | severity | what and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection_adopted` | `satz adopt <estate> --execute --import` | error | Google may already hold a policy this pack declares on the organisation, set by an administrator or by default, and an apply that creates a policy that exists stops on 409 POLICY_ALREADY_EXISTS. Run satz adopt once the pack is on, so every live policy is in the state before the apply; with --import it binds this param itself when it has run. |

## Claims

| framework | control | title | kind | witnesses | interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cis-gcp 5.0 | 6.6 | Cloud SQL IAM database authentication enabled | implements | `google_org_policy_policy.custom_cisCloudSqlIamAuthentication` | A Cloud SQL instance is created or updated only with IAM database authentication on (PostgreSQL and MySQL; SQL Server has no such flag). |
| cis-gcp 5.0 | 6.9 | Cloud SQL deletion protection enabled | implements | `google_org_policy_policy.custom_cisCloudSqlDeletionProtection` | A Cloud SQL instance is created or updated only with deletion protection enabled. |

**What the controls ask** (this project's paraphrase from the catalog — never the framework's own text):

- **Cloud SQL IAM database authentication enabled** (cis-gcp 5.0 §6.6) — Database users of PostgreSQL and MySQL instances sign in with IAM identities.
- **Cloud SQL deletion protection enabled** (cis-gcp 5.0 §6.9) — A Cloud SQL instance cannot be deleted while its deletion protection is on.

**Manual duties** (a control stays *partial* until each is attested):

- `existing-instances` (cis-gcp 5.0 §6.9) — The constraint does not reach instances created before it: enable deletion protection on each existing instance.
- `existing-instances` (cis-gcp 5.0 §6.6) — The constraint does not reach instances created before it: set the flag on each existing PostgreSQL and MySQL instance.

Not every resource this pack contributes is a witness:

- `google_org_policy_custom_constraint.cis_sql_iam_authentication` — contributed, but no claim names it.
- `google_org_policy_custom_constraint.cis_sql_deletion_protection` — contributed, but no claim names it.

## Notes

<!-- notes:start — hand-written, kept across `satz doc-packs` -->

Custom constraints are checked when an instance is created or updated, never against one that already exists: an estate's current instances keep running and fail their next update instead. Prowler has no check for either control, so `report-compliance` is the only thing that reports them. CIS 5.0 only — 4.0 has no equivalent control.

<!-- notes:end -->
